vectors.name: valid-attestation
vectors.description: A well-formed attested claim. Signature verifies; weight derives to the values shown.

vectors.name: tampered-value
vectors.description: Signed honestly, then the claimed location was edited. MUST be rejected.

vectors.name: wrong-pubkey
vectors.description: The signature block names a different key than the one that signed. MUST be rejected.

vectors.name: declared-confidence
vectors.description: Carries an author-declared confidence. MUST be rejected even though the signature is valid.

vectors.name: missing-required-fields
vectors.description: Validly signed, but missing claim.subjectKind and method.observedFrom. MUST be rejected, not rendered with gaps.

vectors.name: coarse-timing
vectors.description: Timing known only to one week against a 24h window. Precision must drop below 1.

vectors.name: enumeration-census
vectors.description: A count from a complete enumeration of one authoritative register. Weighed on completeness, not corroboration.

vectors.name: enumeration-no-boundary
vectors.description: An enumeration with no stated boundary. A count nobody can re-run is rejected outright.

vectors.name: retraction-valid
vectors.description: A well-formed retraction. Published to the claim's own d tag, so the withdrawal propagates through the mechanism the claim did.

vectors.name: retraction-no-note
vectors.description: A retraction without a note. Withdrawing a wrong claim quickly matters more than explaining it well.

vectors.name: retraction-unknown-reason
vectors.description: A retraction whose reason the format does not define. The withdrawal still stands.

vectors.name: relayed-sources
vectors.description: Three sources, all relayed through one aggregator. Corroboration is discounted; the raw sourceCount is unchanged.

vectors.name: canonicalization-edge
vectors.description: Non-ASCII subject, keys deliberately out of alphabetical order in the source. Tests the canonical stringifier, not the signature.

vectors.name: missing-modality
vectors.description: No method.modality. MUST be rejected — how a thing was observed is not optional and MUST NOT be guessed.

vectors.name: unknown-modality
vectors.description: A modality outside the registered vocabulary. MUST be rejected rather than coerced to unknown.

vectors.name: missing-weak-backing
vectors.description: No method.weakBacking. MUST be rejected — an absent array is not the same statement as an empty one.

vectors.name: declared-weak-backing
vectors.description: A conformant claim naming its own unreproducible input. Accepted, and weighs exactly the same as valid-attestation.

vectors.name: modality-not-a-ranking
vectors.description: Same claim, modality in_person instead of primary_record. Weight is UNCHANGED — the vocabulary describes, it does not rank.

vectors.name: method-credit
vectors.description: Cites another node's method. Accepted, and weighs exactly the same as valid-attestation.

vectors.name: partial-method-credit
vectors.description: derivesFrom present but missing `specification`. MUST be rejected — an unfollowable citation is worse than no citation.

vectors.name: underivable-weight
vectors.description: All required fields present and well-formed, but parameters.windowHours is missing so the published facts yield no usable weight. MUST be rejected.

vectors.name: case-adjudication
vectors.description: A human adjudication of a case, published as an attested claim. A consumer that has never seen this algorithm MUST still derive a weight: nothing in the derivation reads `algorithm`.

vectors.name: case-adjudication-no-distance-threshold
vectors.description: The same claim, checked for what it does NOT carry. `distanceThresholdKm` is absent because nothing matched by distance; a consumer MUST NOT treat its absence as zero, nor require it.

vectors.name: case-adjudication-unaddressed-contradictions
vectors.description: An adjudication that left recorded contradictions unanswered. Valid, weighable, and it says so in `weakBacking` rather than in the counts alone.

vectors.name: refutation
vectors.description: A well-formed refutation. Weighable by the same derivation as the claim it contests, and addressed by WHICH claim — author, subject, attribute and the exact publishedAt, every component percent-encoded.

vectors.name: refutation-unencoded-timestamp
vectors.description: The address of the same refutation, stated in full. An implementation that leaves the ISO timestamp raw splits a four-part identifier into six on its own colons, files the contest where nobody looks, and the claim stays uncontested with no error anywhere.

vectors.name: refutation-without-method
vectors.description: A refutation carrying no method. MUST be rejected: without one the cheapest possible message — "wrong" — outweighs expensive evidence, and refutation becomes a denial-of-service on truth.

vectors.name: refutation-unaddressed
vectors.description: A refutation that will not say WHICH version it contests. MUST be rejected: without publishedAt it applies to every later revision of the slot, including one that fixed the very problem being refuted.
